summary:
Neuschwanstein is built as a code generator: build.mjs runs one module per part, from the rock crag to the finishing details. It writes build.nbt (112x76x52, spire top y=75) via a temp file and mv.
Every roof is a preset: tower-cap for all cones and pyramids, cottage for the Knights' House, civic overridden to a steep slate gable for the Palas. Each had a dry-run first and none printed a warning.
Windows come from one `archWindow` helper, caps from one `turretCap`, cornices from one `corniceRing`. Palette: calcite walls, sandstone trim, red brick gatehouse, dark-slate roofs.
`mcd check` reports no floating blocks and the castle is walkable end to end. I looked at all four sides and the closeups. plan.md, elements.md and gaps.md are written, and the plan checklist is ticked.
elements: Palas: a 45x16 calcite block with a steep dark-slate gable roof (cross-gabled front wing, dormers, brick chimneys, iron-bar crest). The gable ends are crow-stepped with sandstone slab coping and a lightning-rod finial. It has three rows of glazed pointed windows on every face, sandstone pilasters on the south face, and a corbelled balcony with a diorite-wall balustrade and a door.
Stair turret: a tall slender round calcite cylinder (radius 3) with spiral arrow slits and a corbel ring. A tower-cap cone on dark slate ends in a lightning-rod finial at y=75, the highest point.
Slender round turrets: nine radius-2 calcite cylinders with corbelled necks and tall tower-cap cones. They stand on the Palas corners, the wing corners, the Knights' House and the Bower.

Square main tower: calcite shaft with a gallery (upside-down stair corbels, slab ring, diorite-wall railing) and a smaller upper stage under a steep pyramid slate roof. A west door opens onto the upper court.

Gatehouse: bricks with smooth_quartz trim, a crenellated parapet, a pointed arch through to a tunnel, and a half-raised iron-bar portcullis. It has three arched windows, lantern posts, and light-blue wall banners with white rhombus patterns. A fence flagpole with a banner stands on the roof, and a stone-brick stair causeway leads up to it.
Flanking gate towers: two round calcite cylinders (radius 4) with spiral arrow slits and tall tower-cap cones, each with a dormer.

Courtyards and curtain walls: 2-thick calcite walls with a stone-brick plinth and crenellated parapets, arrow slits and banners. A lower court is paved with stone bricks and cobblestone and has lantern posts, barrels, hay bales and azaleas. A stone-brick retaining wall with buttresses and a grand stair leads up to the upper court, which has paving and a well (water, wall posts, slab roof, chain and hanging lantern).

Knights' House and Bower: the Knights' House is a gabled calcite hall with a slate cottage roof, a stepped north gable, finial, corner turrets, windows and a door. The Bower is a square calcite tower with a very-steep pyramid slate roof, dormers, windows and corner turrets.

Rock crag: a terraced heightfield of stone, andesite, tuff and cobble with stone-brick retaining walls on the cliff edges. It has boulder outcrops, spruce trees on the slopes and moss patches. The castle stands on it as terraces at y=10 and y=16.
polish: Window heads: the pointed top is only a chamfer plus a one-cell spire, so from a distance the windows read as dark rectangles with sandstone sills. They would benefit from a real pointed or hooded arch.
The Palas north-face balcony is small and mostly hidden behind the curtain wall in the front views. It could be bolder and wider.
The spire finials are lightning rods (copper) rather than gold, and the roofs are one slate palette with no variation between caps.
Interiors are hollow: there are no rooms or floors, only partition walls so the windows don't see sky. The gate tunnel has portcullis bars but no doors.
The rear crag at z=49..51 is a plain grey cliff face, because the grid ends at z=51 and leaves no room for more drama.

The crag is a noisy heightfield with small boulders. It reads as steep and rocky, but taller pinnacles and strata ledges would sell the vertical ridge more. The base is only 10-16 blocks because of the 75-block height cap.
The palette tool still flags trim calcite on calcite walls (the pilaster and cornice sides), the barrels as outliers, and four accent colour families. I left these as deliberate.
Orphan-block warnings remain on cone dormers and spire tips; they are intentional but would still show as 32 in `mcd check`.
